name: Shaul
overview: Shaul was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, uniquely identified as the son of Simeon and a Canaanite woman. He is listed among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, marking him as part of the foundational generations of Israel in the biblical narrative. His descendants, known as the Shaulites, are noted in the census of the tribe of Simeon.
namesAndTitles: The name Shaul means 'asked' or possibly 'dedicated to God,' reflecting a Hebrew origin and indicating a name given by his parents rather than directly by God. This name situates him within the cultural and spiritual heritage of Israel.
familyAndRelationships: Shaul is explicitly recorded as the son of Simeon, one of the twelve sons of Israel. Additionally, he is inferred to be the son of Shallum according to 1 Chronicles 4:25, providing some insight into his paternal lineage within the tribe of Simeon.
scriptureSignificance: Shaul's significance lies in his place within the genealogy of Israel as a son of Simeon who migrated to Egypt, contributing to the growth of the Israelite people during their sojourn. The mention of the Shaulites in the census highlights the establishment of his lineage within the tribe, underscoring the continuity of God's covenant people through successive generations.
